Another issue is understanding the implications of our analysis to other types of matrix regularization, such as weighted trace-norm (Salakhutdinov and Srebro (2010)). As to the use of bounded models, we note that although they seem beneficial in our experiments, they can also lead to non-convex optimization problems. While this did not seem to hurt performance in our experiments, it might be more harmful in other datasets of applications. One possible way to enforce boundeded predictions while maintaining convexity is using ∞-norm constraints, as in Thm. 4. Minimizing the average loss with respect to such constraints is a convex optimization problem, and can be done with a generic SDP solver. However, a generic solver won’t scale to large datasets. Thus, designing an efficient convex optimization algorithm, which combines trace-norm and ∞-norm constraints, is a potentially useful, yet non-trivial challenge.
